marks.gloss_en: הכי קאמר: there are knots one is not liable for -- the nose-ring-strap and isterida knots, patur but asur -- and there are knots permitted ab initio -- the robe's openings (= p_reisha_kitra_bizmama, p_reisha_kitra_beisterida, p_zmama_asur, p_isterida_asur, p_mifta_mutar_lechatchila)
the knots for which one is not liable -- which are they? the knot tied to the nose-ring
the mishna: [a woman may tie] the strings of her hairnet [on Shabbat]
the mishna: a woman may tie the opening of her robe [on Shabbat]
כדרב יהודה -- as Abaye ruled for Rav Yehuda's sandals, worn by him and by his child: permitted ab initio

סנדל אסנדל לא קשיא: liable -- Arabs' [sandals] that shoemakers tie; exempt but forbidden -- what they tie themselves; permitted -- a sandal two people go out in (= p_ok_sandal_chayav, p_ok_sandal_patur, p_ok_sandal_mutar)
the baraita that says liable [for a sandal] speaks of Arabs' [sandals], which shoemakers tie
מדקמתרץ רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי יהודה -- since R' Yochanan extends R' Yehuda's view to Shabbat, the halakha follows R' Yehuda
מאי שנא מדרבי ירמיה? -- R' Abbahu let R' Yirmeya wrap a reed on his torn sandal; why must Abaye leave his?
התם לא מינטר, הכא מינטר -- there the sandal would not be guarded, here it is (= p_minatar)
והא מנא הוא, דאי בעינא הפיכנא ליה מימין לשמאל? -- the torn sandal is still a vessel, since it can be worn on the other foot
מדקמתרץ רבי יוחנן אליבא דרבי יהודה, שמע מינה הלכה כרבי יהודה -- and per R' Yehuda an outer strap broken renders the sandal pure, i.e. no longer a vessel (= p_halakha_kerabbi_yehuda)
R' Abbahu to R' Yirmeya, whose sandal strap tore in a karmelit: take a moist reed fit for animal food and wrap it on it
קשיא מנעל אמנעל -- the baraitot on a shoe contradict: liable, exempt but forbidden (p_b_patur), permitted ab initio
קשיא סנדל אסנדל -- the baraitot on a sandal contradict: liable, exempt but forbidden (p_b_patur), permitted ab initio
the mishna: [one may tie] the straps of a shoe and a sandal [on Shabbat]
מנעל אמנעל לא קשיא: liable -- a shoemakers' [knot]; exempt but forbidden -- the Rabbis'; permitted -- the people of Mechoza's (= p_ok_mindal_chayav, p_ok_mindal_patur, p_ok_mindal_mutar)
the baraita that says liable [for a shoe] speaks of a shoemakers' [knot]
השתא פטור אבל אסור קא קשיא לי, חייב חטאת קאמרת לי?! -- on weekdays too he and his child both wear the sandal, so its knot is not permanent; Abaye: אי הכי, מותר לכתחילה
Rav Yehuda: even 'exempt but forbidden' would be difficult for me, and you say 'liable'?! -- because on weekdays too sometimes I go out in it and sometimes the child does
a sandal whose two ears or two straps broke, or whose whole sole was removed, is pure
והתנן: חלצה של שמאל בימין חליצתה כשרה -- a shoe unfit for its foot still serves for chalitza, so 'not for chalitza, for it is not a vessel' cannot be the Rabbanan's (source p_mishna_smol_bayamin)
the mishna: if she removed the left [shoe] worn on the right foot, her chalitza is valid

אימר דאמרינן חלצה של שמאל בימין חליצתה כשרה, היכא דלמילתיה מנא הוא; הכא למילתיה לאו מנא הוא, דהא אמר רבי יהודה נפסקה החיצונה טהור -- אלמא לאו מנא הוא! (against 'but for chalitza it is a vessel'; cites p_r_yehuda_chitzona_tahor)
read [R' Yochanan's memra]: and likewise concerning chalitza
